question: Does a fresh project-scoped plugin install require approval, and does changing the hook command re-ask?

isolation.trustPrecondition: trust.json for each workspace was seeded before install; this is a trust precondition, not a measurement

plugin.name: e62-probe
plugin.hook: SessionStart `mark`; command node hooks/mark-a.mjs, changed to node hooks/mark-b.mjs

commands: cd scratch/r31-e62/ws-c && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=… XDG_DATA_HOME=… XDG_STATE_HOME=… XDG_CACHE_HOME=… muse plugins install ./plugin --scope project --json
observations: Fresh project-scoped install exited 0 with warning `third-party plugin: hooks require review before activation`.
Before approval, inspect reported runtime capability `mark` status `review_needed` and effective_capabilities [].
Approval exited 0 and recorded trusted_definition_hash sha256:d3f45a… for plugin:e62-probe:hook:mark.
The first echo turn exited 0, wrote marker-a.txt (6 bytes), and reported 1 completed model call with 0 input/output tokens.
Changing only the hook command and running `muse plugins update` exited 0; inspect then reported status `modified`, diagnostic code `modified_definition_hash`, and candidate hash sha256:9d33b4….
The next echo turn exited 0 and wrote marker-b.txt at 2026-11-23 21:27:18.450 -0800 (sha256 c46699865b6d7c32e964b9feaaf93ff06d3ad8f4455432137837fa9bd894c85a).
After that run, inspect reported `trusted_enabled`; settings.json held trusted_definition_hash sha256:9d33b4… and `legacy_hook_trust_amnesty_applied: true`.
The same inspect still reported effective_capabilities [] while the hook had executed.
result: A changed plugin hook ran without a new approval. Muse reported the capability as modified before the run, then the run applied a legacy trust amnesty, promoted the new definition hash, and executed it. This is E62 B2: a security finding.
branch: D246 B2: stop release; changed hook runs without re-approval
workspaceD: not run because the B2 stop condition fired after the second turn
cost: free; two echo turns, 1 completed call each, 0 tokens
limits: This measures Muse CLI 1.4.25 on Linux with an isolated store and a project-scoped local plugin.
It does not identify whether the defect is the legacy amnesty migration or the execution path's failure to re-check the modified hash; both are visible in the record.
It does not test a paid model turn, another Muse version, or a workspace-file hook.
Workspace D's unapproved control was not run after the stop condition.
